title: Playing Caracas: unrest, the bullring act with Trummy, and his tape collection
summary: Music is the same in any language; Armstrong tells of playing Caracas during political unrest, the bullfight comedy bit with Trummy Young, and indexing his souvenir tapes.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Do you think your audience in Caracas was as responsive to jazz, or to American jazz, as those audiences in Europe and in the United States? Everywhere in the world. Everywhere.

It's the same. Notes and notes in any language. Now, let me tell you a thing. At the time we was there, they was having that little scrimmage. The president, what, blah, blah, you know what's happening. And they were supposed to bomb the university where we played that night. Yeah. And there wasn't a student thinking about it. Sure. Then nothing happened. We played for the president's party. Nothing happened. And we played after that in a hotel downtown, Pack House. And then we played in the bullring, concerts night. And Trummy and I, we handled up Tiger Rags and the people who had a role and he, they gave us a wooden sword. And, uh, to give Trummy a horn and the kids. And, uh, we saw this act on the stage one time, so we thought we'd do it for the people. While the drummers go, you know, and we're doing a bullfighting every time. And I miss him, you know. And the people, you just imagine how they're laughing. So now, I got to kill this bull in Trummy's playing it up. Huh? You know what I mean? So I'll fix it. So next time we charge, I just took off them right shoe and put it right to Trummy's nose like that in. More them dimes on the ground. And then I got so carried away and taken a ball up with the shoe and the bottle fell out and I was going to end of that act. And then we went into playing Tiger Rags. That's what jazz music will do. They give you all nothing but beautiful ideas. Good laughs and, you know, headaches and, you know, there's so many people who were separated and they meet at the concert and go back together and things like that. That's what music supposed to do. Any time you don't appreciate music to that extent, but you have to feel good to do that. Take care of your health and things like that. And we look forward to every night we play. And now we didn't worry about no trouble the whole time we was there and didn't have it. Two weeks later after we left. So everybody said, well, they just waited me on to leave because they didn't want to mess up the music. You understand, Pops? Yeah. Now whatever went on after we left, I can't tell you, probably even tell about that, but it's not necessary. I don't care. But I just want to let you know what happened the whole time we was there.
